items.readable_text:
Content:
There are many ways to measure time. Some important conversions for units of time are as follows:

Content:
- [MATH: 1] week = [MATH: 7] days
- [MATH: 1] day = [MATH: 24] hours
- [MATH: 1] hour = [MATH: 60] minutes
- [MATH: 1] minute = [MATH: 60] seconds

Content:
Time is typically measured using clocks, and we can use clocks to visualize equivalent units of time.

Content:
For example, the image below shows a complete revolution of the seconds hand on a stopwatch. It takes precisely one minute (or [MATH: 60] seconds) for this hand to complete one full rotation.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/bbf391d098eec310007ce354ad34c0f7]

Content:
Let's get some practice at converting between different units of time.

items.title: Converting From Weeks to Days

key_prerequisites.name: Multiplying Whole Numbers Ending in Zeros

sections.normalized_html: Maria bought her cell phone [MATH: 9] weeks ago. How many days have passed since she purchased her cell phone?
sections.readable_text: Maria bought her cell phone [MATH: 9] weeks ago. How many days have passed since she purchased her cell phone?

sections.normalized_html:
We need to convert [MATH: 9] weeks into days.

We start with the unit conversion between weeks and days: [MATH: 1 \,\textrm{week} = 7 \,\textrm{days}]

We want to figure out how many days are in [MATH: 9] weeks. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 9{:}] [MATH: 9 × 1week|= 9 × 7days; 9weeks|= 63days]

Therefore, [MATH: 9] weeks equals [MATH: 63] days.

So, Maria bought her cell phone [MATH: 63] days ago.

sections.normalized_html: [MATH: 9] days is equal to how many hours?
sections.readable_text: [MATH: 9] days is equal to how many hours?

sections.normalized_html:
We start with the unit conversion between days and hours: [MATH: 1 \, \textrm{day} = 24 \, \textrm{hours}]

We want to figure out how many hours are in [MATH: 9] days. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 9{:}] [MATH: 9 × 1day|= 9 × 24hours; 9days|= 9 × 24hours]

We can find the value of [MATH: 9\times 24] using an area model:

According to our model,

[MATH: 9\times 24 = 180+36 = 216.]

Therefore, [MATH: 9] days equals [MATH: 216] hours.

Item 5 — Example: Converting From Days to Hours

We can find the value of [MATH: 9\times 24] using an area model:

[IMG: /graphics/f7856f76e3ab91b683c1085d44d9c209]

According to our model,

[MATH: 9\times 24 = 180+36 = 216.]

Therefore, [MATH: 9] days equals [MATH: 216] hours.
